title: Open Oldenburg Conversation Corpus (OOCC): A Corpus of Audio, Video and Body Pose Data in Dyadic Conversations in German
task: five dyadic conversation tasks: free conversation; survival task; would-you-rather; balance-rules; questions game
token_or_recording_size: 7 dyads; ~7 hours raw material; 5 tasks per dyad; 10-minute and selected 2-minute releases
annotation_target: speech-segment timestamps; speaker labels; manually corrected transcripts; word timestamps/durations; articulation rate; acoustic energy; mean pitch; turns; pauses; gaps; overlaps; floor-transfer offset; turn speech rate; backchannels; questions; automatic body landmarks
manual_scope: transcription pipeline used pyannote + Whisper + WhisperX followed by manual correction by native German lab assistants; README explicitly calls 10-minute CSVs manually corrected speech annotations with timestamps
access: public Zenodo; large media files open; use restrictions apply
license: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 plus dataset use conditions
decision_reason: Primary non-singing German production with isolatable human-corrected timing/transcript annotations and public derived production measures; large AV files should remain authoritative references rather than be mirrored.
evidence_summary: Version 2 README documents 14 primary participants recorded July-August 2025; the manual-correction stage follows diarization/transcription/alignment; transcript CSVs include corrected segment timestamps and speech, while the 2-minute derived tables include word timing, articulation rate, energy, pitch and conversational timing measures. MediaPipe body landmarks are automatic and must remain outside the manually grounded core unless linked only as non-core derived covariates.
